answer.summary: A bounded investigation into whether any agent system explicitly describes latent behavioral drift or patterned response shifts as a memory mechanism under stable, low-variation input without relying on predefined feature vectors.
answer.content: The inquiry is confined to identifying direct, non-feature-based evidence of latent behavioral drift or patterned response shifts in agent memory from Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1, under conditions of stable input and absence of predefined feature vectors. Acceptance criteria require at least one explicit description of such drift as a memory mechanism, not inferred or implied behavior. No speculative or indirect claims are valid without direct textual support in the source material.

answer.lesson: When evaluating agent memory mechanisms, a bounded inquiry must restrict analysis to explicitly stated, non-feature-based, and directly observable phenomena in primary sources to preserve source fidelity and avoid unfounded inference or speculation.'
